domain_note: Authenticated bytes are the ASCII domain, one NUL byte, then the canonical payload with signature or mac removed.
authenticator_note: Cases marked authenticator=valid must pass cryptographic verification so the semantic rule under test is actually reached. Cases marked invalid fail verification itself.
warning: Seeds below are published test values and must never sign anything real.
why_this_file_exists: The authority resolves a registration's commissioning_digest against authorisations delivered to it through the commissioning path, never presented by the device. Whether a registration is applied, retained pending, or refused therefore depends on what the authority already holds, which no single wire artifact can express. Each case names the held state, the arriving artifact and its source, and the outcome the contract requires. The artifacts reuse the published registration and authorisation vectors so a verifier that already reproduces those bytes needs nothing new to sign; one registration is newly signed with the published device seed so that a resolved authorisation naming another key can be exercised. Cancellations are signed with the published recovery seed, which the commissioning-ingest registry designates for cancellation.
state_note: receiver_state holds every artifact in full, so the state can be rebuilt through the real entry points. In authority_state_after, retained_registrations and refused_registrations are full state named by digest, while confirmed_epochs lists only the epochs this case newly confirms; an epoch confirmed earlier is never withdrawn. receiver_state.cancellations holds every applied cancellation in full; tombstoned_digests in authority_state_after is full state. dispositions lists every evidence disposition the decision carries, with delivery `response` when it returns in the response to the arriving artifact and `return_set` when the authority commits it to the device's return set; confirmation_delivery says the same of the epoch confirmation, and is null when none is carried.

cases.name: registration_before_authorisation_is_retained
cases.note: No authorisation is held for this device and epoch. The registration verifies and is retained pending: accepted, no confirmation, no gap. The authorisation may still arrive through the commissioning path.

cases.name: authorisation_promotes_retained_registration
cases.note: The registration is already retained pending. The matching authorisation arrives through the commissioning path, not the courier: verify, register, promote and confirm happen in one transaction, and a byte-identical retry of the registration now returns the confirmation.

cases.name: registration_with_held_authorisation_is_applied
cases.note: The authorisation is already held when the registration arrives. Applied and confirmed in the same step.

cases.name: named_authorisation_promotes_its_registration_while_a_sibling_is_held
cases.note: A sibling authorisation for the same device, key and epoch is already held, and a registration naming a different authorisation is retained pending. When the named authorisation arrives it promotes that registration; the sibling decides nothing.

cases.name: unresolved_reference_with_sibling_authorisation_is_retained
cases.note: The authority holds an authorisation for exactly this device, key and epoch, and the registration names a different digest that the authority does not hold. A sibling never substitutes for the named reference, and the named authorisation may still arrive through the commissioning path, so the registration is retained pending: accepted, no confirmation, no gap.

cases.name: resolved_authorisation_names_another_key
cases.note: The registration names the digest of a held authorisation, and that authorisation licenses a different public key. Resolution succeeds and the bound facts disagree: refused as commissioning_digest_mismatch, never applied, no quarantine, no gap.

cases.name: refused_registration_stays_refused_after_its_authorisation_is_revoked
cases.note: The registration was refused commissioning_digest_mismatch because the authorisation it names binds a different key. That authorisation has since been revoked, which marks it rather than forgetting it, and the authority retains the resolution, so the same bytes are refused again, final, whatever the revocation.

cases.name: authorisation_from_courier_is_refused
cases.note: A commissioning authorisation arriving from the device side. It is refused at transport as a type the courier does not carry, before any verifier is invoked, and nothing is retained.

cases.name: revoked_named_authorisation_refuses_an_agreeing_registration
cases.note: The registration names an authorisation that agrees with it in every field, but that authorisation has been revoked. A revoked authorisation licenses nothing: refused commissioning_digest_mismatch, recorded as the terminal refusal, no confirmation and no gap.

cases.name: resigned_registration_with_the_same_binding_is_idempotent
cases.note: A registration is retained pending under its commissioning digest. A later registration names the same digest and the same device, key and epoch, re-signed with a later registered_at_ms. It is accepted idempotently and the first retained bytes are kept.

cases.name: different_binding_under_a_pending_digest_conflicts
cases.note: A registration is retained pending under its commissioning digest. Another registration names the same digest for the same device and key under a different evidence capability profile, so a different epoch and a different binding. It is refused 409 pending_registration_conflict; the first retained bytes remain unchanged and the refused bytes are not retained.

cases.name: disagreeing_named_authorisation_arrival_refuses_the_retained_registration
cases.note: A registration is retained pending, and the authorisation it names then arrives through the commissioning path binding a different key. The authority atomically removes the registration from retention and records commissioning_digest_mismatch as its terminal refusal; no epoch confirmation. A later submission of those exact bytes is refused.

cases.name: applied_registration_retried_after_its_authorisation_is_revoked_returns_the_original_confirmation
cases.note: The registration applied under the authorisation it names and its epoch was confirmed; that authorisation has since been revoked. A byte-identical retry is answered with its retained response, including the original epoch confirmation, before any resolution: revocation never withdraws a confirmation already issued. No new epoch is confirmed and nothing is refused.

cases.name: pending_conflict_applies_once_the_first_registration_is_refused_and_the_authorisation_binds_it
cases.note: A registration was refused 409 pending_registration_conflict while another was retained pending under the same commissioning digest. The named authorisation then arrived binding this registration, so the retained one became a terminal refusal. The same refused bytes, resubmitted, now apply and the epoch confirmation is issued.

cases.name: pending_conflict_is_refused_once_the_authorisation_binds_the_first_registration
cases.note: A registration was refused 409 pending_registration_conflict while another was retained pending under the same commissioning digest. The named authorisation then arrived binding the retained one, which applied. The refused bytes, resubmitted, name a held authorisation that binds another epoch: refused commissioning_digest_mismatch, final for those bytes.

cases.name: registration_accepted_pending_and_since_promoted_is_re_offered_and_returns_its_confirmation
cases.note: The registration was accepted pending, and its named authorisation later arrived and promoted it, so the confirmation was committed on the commissioning path and never delivered. The runtime re-offers the identical bytes, and the authority answers with the retained confirmation. No new epoch is confirmed here, since the promotion already confirmed it.

cases.name: cancellation_removes_the_pending_registration_and_releases_its_place
cases.note: A registration is retained pending under a digest whose authorisation will never arrive. A permitted cancellation naming the same device, epoch and digest removes it from the pending bound, retains its bytes as a terminal refusal, tombstones the digest, and commits artifact_terminal to the device's return set.

cases.name: cancellation_before_registration_terminates_the_later_registration
cases.note: The digest was cancelled before any registration named it. A registration naming it later is refused commissioning_digest_mismatch, terminally, with artifact_terminal in the response.

cases.name: cancelled_authorisation_arriving_later_is_refused_and_revives_nothing
cases.note: The digest is tombstoned and its registration was removed. The cancelled authorisation then arrives through the commissioning path: it is refused cancelled, promotes nothing, and the tombstone stays.

cases.name: cancellation_of_one_digest_leaves_another_pending
cases.note: Two registrations are pending under different digests. Cancelling one removes only it; the other stays pending and keeps its place.

cases.name: cancellation_naming_another_epoch_changes_nothing
cases.note: The registration pending under the digest names another epoch than the cancellation. The cancellation is refused cancellation_mismatch, and the pending registration, its place and the digest are unchanged.

cases.name: cancellation_of_a_held_authorisation_is_refused
cases.note: The authority holds the authorisation the digest names, so nothing is pending under it and revocation is the path. The cancellation is refused authorisation_held and changes nothing.

cases.name: repeated_cancellation_is_idempotent
cases.note: A byte-identical cancellation resubmitted is accepted with the same outcome and changes nothing.

cases.name: distinct_cancellation_of_a_tombstoned_digest_changes_nothing
cases.note: A second, distinct cancellation of a digest already tombstoned for the same device and epoch is accepted and audited, and changes nothing.

cases.name: fresh_reference_registers_after_a_cancellation
cases.note: After a cancellation, a registration under a fresh commissioning reference is retained pending as any registration is, with its retained_pending disposition.

cases.name: pending_conflict_resolves_once_its_digest_is_cancelled
cases.note: A reservation under another epoch held the digest pending, so the genuine registration was refused pending_registration_conflict. The reservation is cancelled and archived; the genuine registration's re-offer then resolves afresh, to a terminal commissioning_digest_mismatch, and a fresh reference repairs it.

cases.name: authorisation_naming_another_issuer_than_its_tombstone_is_refused_terminally
cases.note: The digest was cancelled on the expectation that comm-key-2 would issue it. The authorisation that arrives under that digest was signed by comm-key-1. It is refused 409 cancellation_issuer_mismatch: the authority promotes nothing, keeps the tombstone, records the inconsistency and returns a terminal decision, never a 503 to retry.

cases.name: repeated_issuer_mismatch_stays_terminal_and_idempotent
cases.note: The same authorisation is submitted again under the same mismatched tombstone, with a registration pending under the digest's sibling. The decision is the same terminal 409 cancellation_issuer_mismatch, the tombstone stays, and nothing else changes.

cases.name: fresh_authorisation_under_a_new_digest_proceeds_after_an_issuer_mismatch
cases.note: The mismatched digest stays tombstoned. A newly issued authorisation under a new digest, named by a fresh reference already retained pending, promotes that registration and confirms the epoch as any authorisation does.

cases.name: cancellation_naming_another_expected_issuer_than_the_tombstone_is_refused
cases.note: The digest is already tombstoned for comm-key-1. A cancellation of it naming comm-key-2 as the expected issuer is refused cancellation_mismatch and changes nothing.
